title: 2001 AMC 10 Problem 21
statement: A right circular cylinder with its diameter equal to its height is inscribed in a right circular cone. The cone has diameter \(10\) and altitude \(12,\) and the axes of the cylinder and cone coincide. Find the radius of the cylinder.

solutions.text:
Take an axial cross-section. The cone has base radius \(5\) and height \(12;\) the cylinder appears as a rectangle of width \(2r\) and height \(2r.\)

By similar triangles, \(\dfrac{12-2r}{r}=\dfrac{12}{5},\) so \(5(12-2r)=12r,\) giving \(60=22r\) and \(r=\dfrac{30}{11}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: In an axial cross-section, the cylinder has radius \(r\) and height \(2r\)
